title: Practice routine and recovering low and high notes
summary: He practices daily at work and two hours on weekends, recovered his low notes by adjusting his embouchure, and dislikes extreme high notes.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Lips, teeth and breath: the physical craft of brass playing

blocks.x: And how often do you play now? I mean do you practice or rehearse?

I practice every day almost. Keep the horn down at work during the week. And usually at home I practice about between Saturday and Sunday, maybe two hours. I try to run in two hours. I had a hard time getting low notes out there for a couple of years. Now I've got them back, which I thought I'd never be able to do.
And I can improve my high notes a little now, and I think I got it made.

But the first thing I lost about five years ago was my low notes. I'd go for a low note, nothing would come out of your horn but there. Now usually when you get old you lose your high notes. So I worked on a low note so long long. I finally got them back by tightening up my lip a little bit more at the corners, you know, pulling back against and across the teeth. And now the high notes, I get up around A, they get a little hard for me. But I can play up to A all night long. That's no range though. The new boys go double high C, you know. I don't know. I don't like it. After trumpet passes G above high C, they can have it. Don't sound like anything.
